Write one level of precomputed rows as a pyramid file

Source: R/level.R
a5_write_pyramid_level.Rd

Writes rows that were reduced elsewhere, one level of them, as an a5pyramid file: tiled, boxed and indexed as a5_write_pyramid() writes its levels, but without building anything. Use it where each level is its own file and its rows come from somewhere else, such as a partition of a store whose levels are built from the partition's own leaves, or coarse levels summed from such partitions' partial sums. Such files are in format version 4.

Usage

a5_write_pyramid_level(
  x,
  dest,
  ...,
  data_resolution = NULL,
  ncell = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  weights_type = "uint32",
  reducers = NULL,
  types = NULL,
  codecs = NULL,
  rep_sd = NULL,
  storage = NULL,
  shard = NULL,
  owner = FALSE,
  lod_column = FALSE,
  tile_size = 16384L,
  row_group_size = 131072L,
  compression = c("zstd", "snappy", "none"),
  metadata = NULL,
  threads = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A data frame (an a5R::a5_cell column, value columns and integer matrix columns for vectors) or Arrow data (a uint64 cell column, fixed-size or plain lists of int8 or uint8 for vectors, as DuckDB's TINYINT[]) holding one level's rows, each cell once, at one resolution. Row order does not matter.

dest

Path of the Parquet file to write. An existing file is replaced. The file is written under a temporary name and renamed when complete, so a failed or interrupted write leaves no partial file.

...

Value columns to write, as in a5_pyramid(). Default: every numeric column but ncell and the weights.

data_resolution

The pyramid's leaves' resolution, at least the rows'. Default: the rows', for a file of leaves.

ncell

The name of the column holding the leaves each row summarises, needed for rows coarser than the leaves. NULL (default) for leaves, whose file then has no ncell column.

weights

The name of the column holding each row's summed leaf weights, stored as the weights column (see weights_type), or NULL.

weights_type

The weights column's type. Default: "uint32".

reducers, codecs, rep_sd

How the rows were reduced, recorded in the index for readers, as in a5_pyramid(): not applied.

types

Named character vector of storage types for single columns, such as c(red = "uint8", ndvi = "float32"). See "Column types".

storage

Named character vector of how to store vector columns: "fixed_binary" (default), one fixed-length binary value a row, the smallest footer and the fastest decode; or "list", a Parquet list of the elements, dictionary encoded, which engines such as DuckDB read as an array column (TINYINT[]), as the a5embeddings store keeps its embeddings (format version 4). Such as c(embedding = "list").

shard

NULL, or a list of the shard's tier (from 0), cell (an a5R::a5_cell or 16 hex digits) and resolution.

owner

Whether to add the owner column (needs shard).

lod_column

Whether to store the lod column. Default FALSE: a file of one level needs none, the index gives the level.

tile_size, row_group_size

As in a5_write_pyramid(). The defaults are the embeddings store's: tiles of 16,384 rows in row groups of up to 131,072.

compression

"zstd" (default), "snappy" or "none".

metadata

Named character vector or list of strings to add to the file's key-value metadata, such as a renderer's settings as JSON. The keys "a5pyramid", "a5_index" and "ARROW:schema" are reserved.

threads

Number of threads, or NULL (default) for a5pyramid_threads().

Value

dest, invisibly.

Shards and partial rows

With shard, the file is a shard of a set: the index records its tier and shard cell, and a5_write_pyramid_set_table() can list it. With owner = TRUE the file also has an owner column, each row cell's supercell at the shard resolution (a5R::a5_cell_to_supercell()). The rows of such a shard may be partial: a cell split by the shard's edge has a row in each shard holding some of its leaves, each summarising those leaves alone, and owner names the shard containing the cell's centre. A renderer draws every row; a reader that wants whole cells merges a cell's rows, weighted by the weights column (or ncell), with the column's codec.

See also

a5_write_pyramid_set_table() to list such files as a set.

Examples

library(a5R)
centre <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 10)
cells <- a5_uncompact(a5_spherical_cap(centre, 3000), resolution = 15)
leaves <- data.frame(cell = cells, value = runif(length(cells)), n = 4L)

# a level built elsewhere, here by a5_pyramid(), written as a file
p <- a5_pyramid(leaves, value, lods = 12, weights = "n", weights_type = "uint32")
l12 <- p[p$lod == 12, ]
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
a5_write_pyramid_level(l12, path, value, data_resolution = 15, ncell = "ncell", weights = "n",
                       tile_size = 100, compression = "snappy")
a5_pyramid_info(path)
#> ── a5pyramid file file29673006afc7.parquet ─────────────────────────────────────
#> Size: 1.2 KB (footer 739 B)
#> A5 index: 1.0
#> Leaves: resolution 15, 22 cells
#> LODs: 12
#> Rows: 22
#> Tiles: 1 row groups (tile size 100)
#> Columns: value <float64, mean>
#> Bbox: -3.2269, 55.9282, -3.1195, 56.0411
#> Written by: a5pyramid 0.0.0.9000, a5 crate 1.0.0
